note: Track intervals (theory-ear), step 7 (ladder interval-ears:5): all twelve intervals going down and sounded together, two games at "level": "advanced", then P4, TT and P5 together, narrowed with "set". Missing: interval-ears has no "dir" that mixes directions from one question to the next.

exercise.title: All twelve intervals, down and together
exercise.why: Two notes sounded together give you no first note to count from, so naming all twelve that way makes you hear each interval as one sound.

cells.text:
Press Start in the game below: any of the twelve intervals, with the upper note first.
If two answers sound alike, press Replay in the game and hum from the lower note up to the upper one.
Practice until the 7ths and the tritone come as quickly as the 5th.

Press Start in the game below: the same twelve, with both notes at once.
Listen for the lower note first, then for how far over it the upper one sits.
When you change from down to together, the order is gone but each interval keeps its size.

Press Start in the game below: only P4, TT and P5, both notes at once (P4 for a 4th, TT for the tritone, P5 for a 5th).
The three are a half step apart in size, so listen for the one in the middle, TT, and place the other two under and over it.
Practice until the three no longer sound alike.
